credit_metrics.text: EBITDA declined by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}}, and operating profit fell by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}} after depreciation.
Total debt was stable at {{total_debt@FY2025}}, so gross leverage held at {{gross_leverage@FY2025}} and net cash of {{net_cash@FY2025}} covers the debt several times over.

FFO fell by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, and free cash flow dropped by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} as capex intensity climbed by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}.
Profit for the year fell by {{profit.change@FY2025}} to {{profit@FY2025}}, with the loss of control over the Get2 subsidiary also changing the consolidation scope.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, so cash liquidity declined by {{cash_liquidity.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity@FY2025}}.
Cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, still a sizeable buffer against a debt stock of {{total_debt@FY2025}}.
Net cash of {{net_cash@FY2025}} leaves the balance sheet with no refinancing need, and the group's funding position rests on its own cash rather than drawn facilities.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2025}} to {{passengers@FY2025}}, though traffic growth slowed by {{traffic_growth.change@FY2025}} to {{traffic_growth@FY2025}}.
Aeronautical revenue per passenger increased by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2025}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2025}}, helped by charge adjustments under the price-cap formula.

Costs moved against the top line: personnel expenses rose on collective wage increases and additions to personnel provisions, and the group also booked expenses for environmental measures in the surrounding municipalities.

peer_positioning.text: Flughafen Wien has the lowest net leverage of the airport group ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}), against a peer median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@FY2025}}, and the lowest gross leverage ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@FY2025}}).
Cash liquidity to revenue is the strongest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2025}}), well above the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2025}}.
On profitability the company sits in the middle of the group on EBITDA margin, while capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2025}}.

snapshot.text: Flughafen Wien, the Vienna airport group, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} in FY2025, but write-offs on the abandoned third runway project and higher personnel costs left EBITDA lower.

The EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}, while net leverage moved to net cash of {{net_cash@FY2025}} and gross leverage stayed at {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}.

The point to watch is cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} as capex intensity rose by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}, above the peer median.

watch_items.text: Cash generation: free cash flow fell by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}} and FFO by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}, so the buffer that funds investment is thinner.
